top_choice_rationale: P001 (Mircea Cărtărescu alone) is the only proposal that names a writer, and on the common literary criteria it merits an award. The case rests on a distinctive voice, formal ambition sustained across very large prose structures (Blinding within the Orbitor project, and Solenoid), and imaginative depth in which memory, the body and dream form one metaphysical project. A whole-oeuvre prize can reasonably reward the peaks and overall direction and does not require uniform quality in every late volume. The citation is best scoped to the prose and to what survives translation (architecture, imaginative logic, sustained invention), with poetry left as context because its translation coverage is thinnest. Open uncertainties remain: whether Solenoid reorganizes the earlier project or restates it has not been settled by close reading, and I have not read the Romanian originals or independently verified any source. The six-way round-1 convergence is correlated reasoning from shared public knowledge and is not evidence of merit. P000 (no award) ranks second because no argument has shown the case to be insufficient. If expert reports showed the late fictions mostly restating the earlier ones, my fallbacks would be Zurita and then Adonis, but those are not on this slate.
recusal_note: none apparent from profile. For transparency, my own historical fiction and long residence in Prague and Vienna make the Central European setting geographically close to Cărtărescu's, but this is context and not a tie to him or evidence of preference. Conflicts are disclosed and not adjudicated.
